title: Why Does Spicy Food BURN? 🌶️
description:
You bite one chilli... and your whole mouth is on fire. Except nothing is burning.

Your mouth has heat sensors (a protein called TRPV1) that normally go off at about 43°C and hotter, the kind of heat that scalds. Capsaicin, the molecule that makes chillies hot, fits into that same sensor like a key and switches it on with no heat at all. Your brain gets a real "FIRE!" signal, so it does what it does for real heat: you flush and you sweat. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

Birds don't feel it: their version of the sensor ignores capsaicin. The leading idea is that the burn keeps seed-crunching mammals away, while birds swallow the seeds whole and spread them. Bonus: in a 2019 taste test, milk cooled the burn better than water, and skim milk worked as well as whole.
